subject: Rerank metering & bundle structure — baseline + pilot pricing
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@findwise.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rerank metering + packaging question

Hi Diego,

Quick question on how Redwood bills for rerank/classifier endpoints — we're evaluating a hosted integration and want to map to our existing SLOs and cost model. A couple of details:

- Volume: pilot will be roughly 5M candidate-scoring calls/day, production could go to ~12M.
- Typical request: we send a query and ask your rerank endpoint to score ~50 candidates and return top 5.
- Also have a small multi-label classification workload (batching ~1k texts / call).

Questions: do you meter per "request" or per scored candidate? How do batch calls (multiple candidates in one request) get accounted for? Any baseline rate card or bundle guidance for hosted API customers?

We're trying to build a simple forecast for our finance and would appreciate a baseline estimate + any recommended packaging for a pilot.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week.

— Alex
Director of Search Product
Findwise, Inc.
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@findwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank metering + packaging question

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front and we'll follow with a detailed breakout:

- Metering: Redwood's hosted rerank endpoint typically meters at the per-scored-item level ("per_item_score") when you submit multiple candidates in one API call. So a request scoring 50 candidates counts as 50 scoring units.
- Batches: If you use our batch endpoints (multi-doc payloads) we aggregate per-item counts across the request; batching does not reduce the metered units but it can improve latency and reduce per-token costs through prefix caching and batching efficiencies.
- Classification: Multi-label classification is metered per input x label pair for high-cardinality labels; for common single-label classifiers we meter per input.

I'm looping in Aditya from Pricing who will send a baseline rate card and a suggested pilot bundle you can use to model costs. If that looks good we can schedule a call to walk numbers.

Best,
Diego
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — pleased to connect. Attached is a compact rate card template (Findwise_RateCard_Template_2026-06.xlsx) and a short summary below to help you map to expected spend.

Unit definitions (hosted API):
- per_item_score: one scored candidate returned by a rerank/classifier call. Example: one request scoring 50 candidates = 50 per_item_score units.
- per_query_rerank: an API call where we also include network/compute overhead; used mainly for SLO planning rather than billing math.
- embedding/token charges: apply if you simultaneously request embeddings or text generation.

Baseline public rates (example placeholders, final price depends on commit):
- per_item_score: $0.0009 per scored item (volume tiering applies)
- batch (any request with >1k candidates): 10% off per_item_score effective rate via committed bundles

Tiering suggestions for your volumes (monthly):
- 0–50M items: base price above
- 50M–200M items: 18% discount
- 200M+ items: 30% discount + custom SLA

Pilot recommendation: 6-week pilot, 10k pilot credits (scored-item credits) + a $5k test bucket for integration. If you commit to a 6-month $50k/month reserved package we can extend to 20k pilot credits and a 20% discount on the first 3 months.

Examples:
- Pilot (5M items/day * 6 days): ~270M per_item_score units across 6 weeks — recommended to run a capped pilot at 25% volume or negotiate a lower per-item pilot rate.
- Production estimate (12M items/day): ~360M items/month -> at 18% discount indicative bill ~$X (see attached for exact math).

Please review the attached spreadsheet; Laura is on the thread for contracting and invoicing details. Happy to hop on a numbers call tomorrow or early next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex@findwise.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank metering + packaging question — baseline rate card attached

Thanks Aditya — a couple clarifications after reviewing the sheet:

- If we send a single request that scores 50 candidates but we only return top 5, do we still pay for 50 units? (Your note implies yes, but want to confirm.)
- For multi-label classification: we have a case where each text is scored against 12 labels (sparse selection). Do we get charged 12 per input?
- For the pilot math: your example assumes running full production volumes. We planned a smaller pilot (10% of pilot-day volume) to validate quality and latency. Is there a small-volume pilot rate or should we just use pilot credits?

Appreciate the clarity — if you can confirm the per-item semantics and a sample invoice for a 6-week small pilot (numbers for both the 10% pilot and a full capped 25% pilot) that would be great.

— Alex
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@findwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank metering + packaging question — baseline rate card attached

Alex — quick confirmations and an offer to keep things simple:

- Yes: per_item_score is counted for every candidate scored server-side, independent of how many you return. So 50 scored = 50 units billed.
- Multi-label: charged per input x label pair for large label sets. For sparse label sets we can provide a capped-rate option (e.g., charge as if 4 labels per input for pricing predictability) — we typically offer this on committed packages.
- Small pilot: we recommend using pilot credits. I've proposed two pilot paths in the attached rate card: a small-volume pilot (10k scored-item credits) and a scaled pilot (25k scored-item credits + 20% pilot discount).

Offer for Findwise: if you sign a 6-month reserved package at $50k/month (month-to-month invoice, 30-day SLA), Redwood will provide:
- 20% discount on per_item_score for the first 3 months
- 20k scored-item pilot credits up front
- Contract-ready SOW draft attached (Findwise_SOW_Draft_2026-06.pdf)

Next steps: Laura will send the contract template and a short invoice example in a separate email. If this looks good I can lock the HubSpot deal (link below) and book a 30-min intake call to walk the integration checklist.

Best,
Diego
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
